findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the function name in the auto-discovery grounding note from `_find_skill_files` to `find_skill_files` (no leading underscore), per scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py:51.
evidence: Plan text: "globs `**/SKILL.md` under `examples/agent-skills` (`_find_skill_files`, `:52-55`)"
scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py:51: `def find_skill_files(root: Path) -> list[Path]:` — no leading underscore
search for `_find_skill_files` returns (no matches); `find_skill_files` is defined at :51 and called at :154
The glob behaviour and line range (:52-55) the plan relies on are otherwise accurate — only the symbol name is wrong
findings.finding: The plan names the skill-discovery helper as `_find_skill_files` (leading underscore), but the actual function in scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py is `find_skill_files` with no leading underscore.
findings.location: Plan grounding section: 'A new skill directory is auto-discovered by a CI gate' — `scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py` ... `_find_skill_files`, `:52-55`
scenarios: A reader following the citation to confirm auto-discovery greps for `_find_skill_files` and finds nothing, undermining confidence in the grounding
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `_find_skill_files` with `find_skill_files` in the 'auto-discovered by a CI gate' paragraph.

findings.checklist_item: Specify WHO or WHAT measures main's net LOC and mechanism count a week after a tidy run and what happens when it is non-negative — otherwise the week-later metric is declared but never acts on the run it judges.
evidence: Plan: 'the run is measured by main's LOC and mechanism count a week later, not by tickets filed'
AC only requires the skill to DECLARE the metric ('Verified by reading the skill'), not that any process measures it.
SKILL.md:121 'this is a personal skill with no post-launch tuning loop' — kept unchanged by the split.
ticketization.md:47 ends the pipeline at ticket filing; edits 'happen later, when someone works a ticket' — no step revisits main a week on.
findings.finding: The headline success metric — 'measured by main's LOC and mechanism count a week later, not by tickets filed' — names no measuring actor and no corrective loop. The skill is a prompt artifact that ends at ticketization; nothing in the plan (or the kept SKILL.md, which states at :121 there is 'no post-launch tuning loop') measures main a week later or acts on a run that failed to net-reduce.
findings.location: Then change the tidying janitor's contract (success-metric bullet) + ACs 'declares a success metric measured on main a week later'
scenarios: A tidy run files its capped tickets; a week later main's LOC/mechanism count rose (tickets added net complexity, like the 08-29 run the plan cites); no part of the skill or process detects this, so the self-defeating pattern the split targets recurs undetected.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) make the measurement a concrete step (e.g. a follow-up operator checklist item or a scripted census against scripts/_mechanism_delta on the post-landing SHA) with a stated consequence for a failed run, or (b) reframe the metric as a per-ticket precondition the tidy skill itself can enforce at ticketization (each ticket must name a net deletion), since a prompt artifact cannot observe main a week later.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion that the tidying janitor also retains the KEEP four (blind verification, prior-decision checking, one-at-a-time approval, discovery), or explicitly state which of them do not apply to the deletion-only skill.
evidence: 'KEEP: discovery, blind verification, prior-decision checking, one-at-a-time approval. Those four are what make the skill trustworthy and none of them is implicated.'
Defect-audit AC: 'The defect audit retains discovery, blind verification, prior-decision checking, and one-at-a-time approval.'
No tidying-janitor AC covers blind verification / prior-decision checking / one-at-a-time approval — only SHA discovery is restated for it
findings.finding: The KEEP section retains discovery, blind verification, prior-decision checking, and one-at-a-time approval across the split, but only the defect audit has a covering acceptance criterion for those four; the tidying janitor has no criterion asserting it retains blind verification, prior-decision checking, or one-at-a-time approval (its ACs cover only SHA-discovery, cap, metric, no-gates, atomic-condensation).
findings.location: 'The change — modify, not discard' KEEP list vs the tidying-janitor acceptance criteria
scenarios: The tidying janitor ships without blind verification or one-at-a-time approval, yet every AC still passes
findings.suggested_fix: Add: '- [ ] The tidying janitor retains blind verification, prior-decision checking, and one-at-a-time approval (discovery is the SHA-based variant above). Verified by reading the skill.'

findings.checklist_item: State how the tidying janitor's Phase-2 verification is retuned (or replaced) so deletion/collapse findings survive — e.g. scoring on debt_impact/optionality rather than prod_impact+harm_reachable — since the plan itself diagnoses the current floor as selecting for defects not complexity.
evidence: Plan gap #1: 'The Phase 2 floor selects for defects, not complexity... Defect remediation adds mechanism more often than it removes it.'
Plan KEEP: 'blind verification' is listed as one of the four kept, trustworthy parts.
verification.md:49 'When harm_reachable is no the finding is not dropped — it is RECLASSIFIED as HARDENING' and :162 'DROP ... OR impact < 0.5'
verification.md:118-121 prod_impact=none for a pure docs/removal edit; impact floors near 0.25 for removals with no blast/likelihood
The contract-change bullet list changes outputs, cap, metric, gates, SHA window, atomicity — but nothing retunes or replaces the Phase-2 floor the plan identified as the defect-selecting mechanism.
findings.finding: The plan's own root-cause diagnosis (gap #1: 'the Phase-2 floor selects for defects, not complexity') is never resolved by the 'change the contract' list — the tidying janitor KEEPS blind verification unchanged, but that verification's floors (`impact >= 0.5`, `harm_reachable` demonstration, verification.md:49 reclassifying no-reachable-harm findings as HARDENING, and `prod_impact = none` for pure removals) are built to find defects and will DROP the deletion/collapse findings the tidy skill is supposed to admit.
findings.location: The change — modify, not discard (KEEP list) + Then change the tidying janitor's contract
scenarios: A dead-code or spent-optionality deletion finding scores prod_impact=none, fails harm_reachable, is reclassified HARDENING or falls below impact>=0.5, and is dropped — so the tidy skill produces few or no admissible deletions despite correctly discovering them.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a contract bullet specifying the tidy skill's survival criterion for a deletion/collapse finding (debt_impact + net-LOC/optionality, not harm_reachable), and say explicitly which of verification.md's floors/sub-questions are dropped or re-weighted so removals are not reclassified HARDENING or sunk below impact>=0.5.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the tidying janitor skill define or explicitly reference the closed 'mechanism' taxonomy (the seven kinds) it censuses for 'mechanism delta'/'mechanism count', with an AC verifying the skill carries or cites that vocabulary.
evidence: Plan: 'judged at review by net LOC and non-positive mechanism delta'; 'measured by main's LOC and mechanism count a week later'

dep fe94 defines the closed seven-kind list (lock, env_var, config_key, feature_flag, ci_gate, autouse_fixture, test_helper) in .rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-net-mechanism.md and scripts/_mechanism_delta/markers.py — a plan-review rubric and ratchet script, NOT a vocabulary the janitor SKILL reads
search_files over examples/agent-skills shows 'mechanism' there always denotes a bug's CAUSAL mechanism, never the complexity census — so no inherited vocabulary exists for the executor
Plan asserts fe94 'formalizes the same measure' but fe94's output is consumed at claim-time plan review, not by the janitor skill at discovery/measurement time
findings.finding: The tidying janitor's review criterion and success metric ('non-positive mechanism delta', 'main's ... mechanism count a week later') reference a 'mechanism' vocabulary that is never defined or pointed to from within the skill; the closed seven-kind taxonomy exists only in scripts/_mechanism_delta/ and the plan-review rubric from dep fe94, and no acceptance criterion requires the tidy skill to enumerate or cite it.
findings.location: Plan §'The change — modify, not discard' (tidying-janitor contract) and AC 'declares a success metric ... net LOC and mechanism count'
scenarios: An operator runs the tidy janitor; at review (and at the week-later census) the executor must compute 'mechanism count' but the SKILL.md gives no enumeration of what counts as a mechanism
Two different executors census different sets, so 'non-positive mechanism delta' is not reproducible
findings.suggested_fix: Add an acceptance criterion requiring the tidy skill body to enumerate the seven counted mechanism kinds inline (or cite the net-mechanism rubric/ratchet as the authoritative source), and state the list is closed — mirroring fe94's self-contained-taxonomy requirement so the janitor's measure and the plan-review criterion cannot diverge.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define what a 'collapse'/'condensation' is for the tidying janitor and reconcile it with the inherited 'never edits code' rule — stating whether collapses are proposed as tickets or performed directly, and the boundary against ordinary edits.
evidence: Plan: tidying janitor 'whose only admissible outputs are deletions and collapses'; 'a condensation is one atomic change or is not done'
Inherited/KEPT rule SKILL.md:68 'Never edit code. The pipeline emits a plan and tickets.' — a collapse/condensation is itself a code edit
Plan: tidy run is 'capped at a handful of tickets, each landable in one session' (implies tickets, not direct edits) but never resolves this against 'collapses' as an output
findings.finding: The admissible-output vocabulary ('deletions and collapses'; 'a condensation is one atomic change') is never distinguished from the inherited 'never edits code' rule, and the plan does not state whether the tidy janitor performs collapses itself or files them as tickets — leaving the executor no rule to classify a proposed change as in- or out-of-vocabulary.
findings.location: Plan §'SPLIT into two skills' (tidying janitor admissible outputs) and §'Plan grounding' ('Never edits code' moves with the split)
scenarios: An executor finds a candidate condensation and cannot tell whether merging two near-duplicate helpers is an admissible 'collapse' or a prohibited 'edit'
Reviewer applying the AC 'admissible outputs are deletions and collapses only' has no definition of 'collapse' to check a finding against

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State a concrete per-run ticket cap (a specific number or a stated default the executor applies unless told otherwise) rather than 'a handful'.
evidence: 'a run is capped at a handful of tickets, each landable in one session'
AC: 'It declares a per-run ticket cap. Verified by reading the skill.'
'a handful' is a defaultable gap under E2 signal (2) — implicit size limit
findings.finding: The per-run ticket cap is left as 'a handful of tickets' with no concrete number; the AC only requires that 'a per-run ticket cap' be declared, so an executor writing the skill must invent the number.
findings.location: The change section ('capped at a handful of tickets') and AC 'It declares a per-run ticket cap.'
scenarios: Executor picks 3, reviewer expected 5-7; the skill's cap is contested at review
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'a handful of tickets' with an explicit default, e.g. 'at most 5 tickets per run', and update the AC to assert the declared cap is that number (or a named default).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the week-later metric handles not-yet-landed tickets and isolates the run's own net-LOC/mechanism contribution from unrelated concurrent merges (e.g. a per-ticket diff delta rather than a whole-main snapshot).
evidence: Plan: 'the run is measured by main's LOC and mechanism count a week later, not by tickets filed'
Plan's own premise is 'a deliberate pause between features' — so other features may land in the same week, confounding a whole-main delta
No stated protocol for the not-yet-landed case or for attribution
findings.finding: The 'measured on main a week later' success metric specifies no fallback for an incomplete sub-step: it does not say what the measurement means if the run's tickets are not landed within the week, nor how the run's net-LOC/mechanism contribution is isolated from unrelated features merged in the same window.
findings.location: Plan §'The change — modify, not discard' and AC 'declares a success metric measured on main a week later'
scenarios: A tidy run's deletions land but an unrelated feature adds 2,000 LOC the same week; whole-main LOC rises, so the metric reads as failure for work that succeeded
Tickets slip past the week boundary; the executor/reviewer has no defined reading of the metric

findings.checklist_item: State how rebar-tidy obtains the four KEPT phases — shared reference vs byte-identical copy — and account for the resulting net-LOC delta so the split does not silently inflate the metric the tidying janitor is judged by.
evidence: Plan: 'KEEP: discovery, blind verification, prior-decision checking, one-at-a-time approval' to be present in both skills
Plan grounding: existing skill is '7 files, 1,014 lines'; the kept phases live in substantial files (phases/discovery.md, verification.md, approval.md)

tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py:27-32 shows the repo's established mechanism is byte-identical per-skill COPIES (shared/test-design.md), i.e. duplication is the in-repo convention — so rebar-tidy would likely copy, adding LOC
The tidying janitor's own stated success metric is "main's LOC ... a week later" — a deliverable whose first act may duplicate hundreds of prompt lines should account for that cost
findings.finding: The plan keeps four phases (discovery, blind verification, prior-decision checking, one-at-a-time approval) in BOTH skills but does not specify whether rebar-tidy duplicates the existing janitor's phase files or shares them, leaving the net-LOC cost of the split unquantified against the deliverable's own success metric.
findings.location: 'The change — modify, not discard' / KEEP paragraph and SPLIT bullets; AC list
scenarios: rebar-tidy/ is created by copying discovery.md/verification.md/approval.md from rebar-janitor, roughly doubling those phases' LOC and silently inflating the very net-LOC metric the skill is judged by
A reviewer cannot verify the split reduced (or at least did not grow) complexity because the plan never states the shared-vs-duplicated phase strategy
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence specifying whether the four kept phases are shared (referenced) or copied into rebar-tidy/, and if copied, note the one-time LOC cost and exclude it from the week-later net-LOC baseline; add an AC asserting the chosen strategy.
